Life is strange sometimes. I don't know how the hell I got here. In Germany I mean. I also have no idea what it is I'm really doing here. On one hand I thought I was chasing a dream, to live in a new place, completely new from anything I'd ever known before. I've come to find that after the novelty wears off, it's really just like any other place really. Sure the culture is different, what's considered rude is measured by entirely different standards, but I've come to discover that people are all people, at heart we're all the same. Sometimes this is reassuring, other times not so much.

Now that the novelty has worn away, I feel entirely purposeless here. I've been exposed for just being a carbon based life form exchangin oxygen for carbon-dioxide. I guess to come to the point, I've always wanted to find a special purpose. Some of us have found ours already. Some of us have found this special feeling in becoming a parent, or in becoming a pilot, climbing a mountain, so on and so forth. I traveled an ocean in search of mine, and I still haven't found it. I mean, that's ok that I haven't found it yet, but as I get older I grow more worried that I might never discover it.

Perhaps that's the point though. Perhaps it's merely an illusion, the idea of finding a special purpose. Just maybe, the journey istelf is the destination after all.

“This material shows that the IRS‘ cover-up began years ago,” said Tom Fitton, president of Judicial Watch. “We now have smoking-gun proof that top officials in the Obama IRS unlawfully harassed taxpayers just to keep them from complaining to Congress about IRS‘ targeting and abuse.
